changes.comment:
Teaches the path types the difference between a value with an addressable interior and one without.

A `Map` or `Set` keeps its contents outside its own enumerable keys, so walking one with `keyof` yielded the names of its *methods*: `byId.get` and `byId.size` were offered as subscribable paths, and a slice holding a plain number autocompleted `toFixed`. None of them could ever fire, because the diff reports such a value at its own path and never descends into it. The new `RootValue` type states that rule once, and `Path` and `Dotted` both defer to it.

`Dotted` now resolves to the empty path for a slice that IS one value, so `{ reducer, property: "" }` type-checks where it can actually fire instead of falling through to the untyped overload. The conditional distributes, so a nullable object slice gets both `""` and its keys — which is correct: it changes at its root when it becomes `null`, and at a leaf otherwise. `PathValue<T, "">` now resolves to `T`, matching what both path readers have always returned for an empty path; it used to say `never`.

No path that resolved before stops resolving. Pinned by membership assertions in the type tests, which name each path individually so a single one appearing or vanishing is a build failure.
